headline: Debora now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing, and is skipping showers out of fear of slipping. Her spouse Kevin, the primary caregiver, reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. She was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing support.
items.verifier_note: Note n002 matches every detail: date, moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independent at last review, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide reported Debora needed hands-on help getting out of the tub. She said she has been skipping showers because she is afraid of slipping.
items.verifier_note: Note n001 matches the date, the hands-on help getting out of the tub, and skipping showers from fear of slipping.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: Note n007 matches the date, Kevin's role, exhaustion and poor sleep, worry about evenings, the respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks. No recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The sertraline start, PHQ-9, pharmacist reconciliation and 4-week recheck are all supported. The claim that no recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes can't be verified from the cited notes. They don't cover the later period, so it is an absence claim the sources can't confirm.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which began 2026-08-01. The most recent dose was on 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows no flu vaccine this season and a most recent dose on 2026-04-25. A dose in April 2026 is odd for the previous season, but the record shows it. The season start of 2026-08-01 is also supported. The statement is essentially supported, but the April dose is oddly timed. Strictly, everything is in the record, so this is arguably fully supported.

questions_for_team: Which bathing supports can start now (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, more home care hours), and how will bathing and hygiene be covered until they are in place?
What respite or evening support can be arranged for Kevin, and who will follow up with him?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck been done? Is a repeat PHQ-9 due, and could fear of slipping and caregiver stress be affecting her mood?
The PT evaluation dated 2026-10-05 was written after a fall entry that was later corrected as a charting error. Does the walker recommendation and twice-weekly PT plan still apply?
When can the influenza vaccine be offered this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the last IDT review date is documented, so all changes are captured since then.
Falls and injuries: count falls, near-falls, and fall-related injuries in the window; check whether any fall occurred while on new sertraline, and review fall-risk screening and home safety notes.

ED visits and hospital admissions: list any ED visits or admissions in the window, reasons, and discharge follow-up status; pay particular attention to chest pain, dyspnea, or COPD exacerbation episodes given ischemic heart disease and COPD.

Medication changes: reconcile starts and stops in the window. Confirm the sertraline start on 2026-09-13 (for depressive symptoms, PHQ-9 of 14) is documented with prescriber, dose, and planned follow-up; check for any new bleeding, bruising, or GI symptoms since it was started, given concurrent clopidogrel.

Cardiac and antiplatelet review: verify adherence to metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, simvastatin, and PRN nitroglycerin; check nitroglycerin refill and use frequency; note any angina episodes documented in the window.

Respiratory review: check albuterol and fluticasone/salmeterol use frequency and refill timing; look for rescue inhaler use increase, oxygen use, or missed doses, since inhaler starts are dated 2026-04-25 and may warrant technique review.
Vitals and weight trend: review blood pressure and heart rate trend (particularly on metoprolol), and weight trend given BMI 30+ and obesity; flag any unintended weight change of note.

Glycemic and thyroid monitoring: check most recent HbA1c or glucose values (prediabetes) and TSH or levothyroxine monitoring status for idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism, noting whether any labs are due in the window.

Pain, mood, and cognition: reassess chronic pain severity and analgesic use; repeat PHQ-9 or equivalent at or after sertraline start and check for side effects or early response; screen cognition if any change is reported; review sleep and appetite.

Function, ADLs, and caregiver/social situation: compare IADL and ADL status to prior review, check attendance at program visits, transportation barriers, caregiver availability or strain, and any care-plan items (advance directive, breast cancer surveillance or survivorship follow-up, vaccines) that are due or overdue.
